platform_notes: All Clover devices in our sheets run Clover's own software (Register, Sale, Orders, Transactions, Tips, Refund, Setup, Dining and Gift cards apps) with the web dashboard; Clover Go is a phone/tablet app (G1 and G2 versions) with an optional card reader. This file covers day-to-day software articles from Clover's help centre that are not linked for logged-out visitors but load publicly by direct URL; it complements clover-operations and clover-hardware.

entries.title: Take a payment in the Register app
steps: On the device, open the Register app.
Add items to the order, then tap Pay.
Choose Pay Full Amount, Split Custom Amount or Split by Items.
Choose the method of payment: Credit/Debit, Cash or Other.
For Credit/Debit, dip or swipe the card, enter the card number by hand, or use contactless if the device has it.
Follow the prompts to complete the payment.
entries.quote: For Credit/Debit, dip or swipe a payment card, manually enter a card number, or use contactless payment (if available on this device).

entries.title: Take a cash payment in the Register app
steps: Open the Register app, add items to the order and tap Pay.
Choose Cash.
Tap one of the cash options, or tap Custom to enter a custom amount.
Follow the prompts to complete the payment.
entries.quote: For Cash, tap one of the cash options, or tap Custom to enter a custom amount.

entries.title: Let customers check out on a Mini or Flex by themselves (secure payment flow mode)
steps: Open the Setup app.
Select Payments.
Select Enable secure payment flow mode.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Select Enable secure payment flow mode.

entries.title: Take a customer-facing payment in the Register app
steps: In the Register app, add items to an order.
Select Pay, then select Charge.
Hand the device to the customer.
The customer selects the tip, inserts, taps or swipes their card, and selects their receipt.
The customer hands the device back when done.
entries.quote: Select Pay, then select Charge.

entries.title: Customer sees a message to return the device to an employee
steps: This appears during customer-facing checkout when the device detects an issue or a duplicate payment.
Take the device back from the customer and deal with the issue shown.
entries.quote: If there are any issues detected during checkout or the device detects a duplicate payment, an error will be shown to the customer instructing them to return the device to an employee.
entries.note: The source does not give the wording of the message or further steps.

entries.title: Take a quick cash payment with Fast Pay With Cash
steps: Open the Register app.
Add items by scanning, searching or selecting.
In the Orders sidebar, under Fast Pay with Cash, choose a cash amount option.
If you tapped Custom, tap one of the payment options on the Pay With Cash screen, then tap Continue.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: In the Orders sidebar, under Fast Pay with Cash, choose a cash amount option.

entries.title: Fast Pay with Cash does not show in the Register app
steps: A manager may need to switch it on.
In the Register app, swipe the screen from the left and tap Settings.
Check the box to Enable Fast Pay with Cash.
entries.quote: Your manager can go to Register Settings (swipe the Register app screen from the left and tap Settings) and check the box to Enable Fast Pay with Cash.

entries.title: Allow Fast Pay With Cash payments to be refunded on the payment screen
steps: Open the Setup app and go to Payment Receipts.
Turn on 'Automatically print customer receipt after each order'.
Turn on 'Skip receipt screen & begin next transaction'.
entries.quote: Payments made with Fast Pay With Cash can be refunded immediately on the payment screen.

entries.title: Turn on Fast Pay With Cash from the Setup app
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Payments.
Tap Enable Fast Pay With Cash.
Preset dollar amounts then show under Fast Pay with Cash in the order summary panel.
entries.quote: Once set up, you'll see predetermined dollar amounts under Fast Pay with Cash in the order summary panel.

entries.title: Turn on Fast Pay With Cash from the dashboard
steps: Log in to your Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Transactions, select Payments.
Select Enable Fast Pay With Cash in Register.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Select Enable Fast Pay With Cash in Register.

entries.title: Split a payment evenly or by custom amounts in the Register app
steps: In the Register app, add items to the order, then tap Pay.
Tap Split Custom Amount.
Tap one of the X Ways buttons and tap Pay, or tap Custom, enter the amount on the number pad and tap PAY.
Choose the payment method and follow the prompts.
Tap Next Payment to take the next part, or tap Pay More Later to save the order.
entries.quote: Tap Next Payment to make the next partial payment, or tap Pay More Later to save the order.

entries.title: Split a payment by items in the Register app
steps: Start in your order in the Register app.
Tap Review Order.
Tap Pay.
Tap the More menu at the upper right.
Tap Split by Items.
Select the items being paid for now, then tap Next.
Choose the method of payment and follow the prompts.
Tap Next Payment for the next part, or Pay More Later to save the order.
entries.quote: Select the items being paid for now, and then tap Next.

entries.title: Save an open order to pay later
steps: Open the Register app.
Add items by scanning, searching or selecting.
In the left panel at the bottom, next to the Pay button, select Save.
Open the Orders app to carry on with the order later.
entries.quote: In the left panel at the bottom next to the Pay button, select Save.

entries.title: Jump from the Register app to the Orders app
steps: Start in the Register app.
At the top right, tap Orders to open the app.
entries.quote: At the top right, tap Orders to open the app.

entries.title: Take a chip card payment in the Sale app
steps: Open the Sale app.
Enter the sale amount, then tap Charge.
If the device asks for an invoice number (or your custom identifier), enter it and tap Continue.
Hand the device to the customer.
If tips are entered on screen, the customer selects the tip amount and inserts their card.
The customer may be asked for a PIN.
When the customer hands the device back, choose how they get their receipt.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: If the Tip entry location is 'Tip on screen', the customer selects the tip amount and inserts their card.

entries.title: Take a contactless (tap) payment in the Sale app
steps: Open the Sale app.
Enter the sale amount, then tap Charge.
If asked, enter an invoice number and tap Continue.
The customer selects the tip amount if tips are on screen, then holds the card or phone over the contactless mark.
The customer may be asked for a PIN.
Choose how the customer gets the receipt.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: the customer selects the tip amount and holds the card or phone over the contactless mark.

entries.title: Take a swipe payment in the Sale app
steps: Open the Sale app.
Enter the sale amount, then tap Charge.
If asked, enter an invoice number and tap Continue.
The customer selects the tip amount if tips are on screen, then inserts, taps or swipes the card.
Choose how the customer gets the receipt.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: You can take a swipe payment card in the Sale app when making a payment.

entries.title: Customer swiped a chip card and the device asks to insert it
steps: This is expected: customers who swipe a chip card are prompted to insert it instead.
Have the customer insert the chip card.
entries.quote: However, if a customer has a chip card, customers who swipe their card are prompted to insert it instead.

entries.title: Where to swipe a card on a Station Duo
steps: Have the customer swipe the card on the Mini terminal facing them.
entries.quote: Note: For Station Duo, have the customer swipe the card on the Mini terminal facing them.

entries.title: Skip PIN entry during a Sale app payment
steps: If the customer is asked to enter their PIN and you want to skip it, tap Skip.
entries.quote: (Optional) Customers may be asked to enter their PIN. To skip entering a PIN, tap Skip.

entries.title: Void a Sale app payment straight after it goes through
steps: When the customer hands the device back after paying, tap Void transaction instead of choosing a receipt option.
entries.quote: Tap Void transaction to void the payment.

entries.title: Sale app payment when tips are written on the paper receipt
steps: Take the payment in the Sale app as usual.
Give the customer the paper receipt to add the tip amount, total and signature.
Enter the tip on the paid transaction afterwards.
entries.quote: If the Tip entry location is 'Tip on paper', provide the customer with a paper receipt to add their tip amount, total, and signature.

entries.title: Device asks for a passcode after every customer payment
steps: This happens when secure payment flow mode is on: once a payment is completed the session signs out.
Enter a valid passcode to take the next payment.
The setting is in the Setup app under Payments: Enable secure payment flow mode.
entries.quote: so that once payment is completed, the session signs out, and a valid passcode must be entered to take the next payment.

entries.title: Take a customer-facing payment in the Sale app
steps: Open the Sales app.
Enter the amount and select Charge.
Hand the device to the customer.
The customer completes the card payment by chip, contactless or swipe.
When the customer is done, enter a passcode to continue.
entries.quote: Once the customer is done, the device requires a passcode to continue with the payment flow.

entries.title: Which Clover devices can take EBT
steps: EBT and SNAP food benefit payments can be taken in the Register or Sale app.
Compatible devices listed by Clover: Clover Mini, Clover Mobile, Clover Flex, Clover Station Duo, Clover Station and Clover Compact.
entries.quote: Clover devices compatible with EBT are: Clover Mini, Clover Mobile, Clover Flex, Clover Station Duo, Clover Station, Clover Compact.

entries.title: Get a device ready to take EBT
steps: On the device, go to the App market and install the EBT app so customers can check their benefit balances.
Check the device is connected to the internet.
Select EBT as an accepted tender type in the Setup app.
To reach the Setup app from the Register app: top-left menu, Settings, then Additional settings.
entries.quote: Select EBT as an accepted tender type on the Setup app.

entries.title: EBT cannot be taken while the device is offline
steps: Check the device is connected to the internet before taking an EBT payment.
Offline EBT transactions are not supported.
entries.quote: Verify that your device is connected to the internet to process EBT transactions; offline transactions are not supported.

entries.title: No tip option on an EBT payment
steps: This is expected: tipping is not allowed for EBT cards.
entries.quote: Note that Tipping is not allowed for EBT cards.

entries.title: Take an EBT payment in the Register app by choosing EBT
steps: Open the Register app.
Add items to the order, then tap Pay.
In the Other section, tap EBT.
Tap Cash benefit or SNAP food benefit, then select Pay.
Insert or swipe the EBT card. For SNAP Food Benefit you can instead tap Manual card entry and enter the card number and expiration date.
Tap Continue.
If cash back is turned on, ask a customer paying with an EBT Cash Benefit Card whether they want cash back and how much.
Ask the customer to enter the EBT PIN on the customer-facing screen, then tap Enter.
Ask the customer to select a receipt option.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: Tap Cash benefit or SNAP food benefit, then select Pay $X.XX.

entries.title: Take an EBT payment in the Register app by charging and swiping
steps: Open the Register app.
Add items to the order, then tap Pay.
Tap Charge on connected device.
Insert or swipe the EBT card.
Ask the customer to select Cash Benefit or SNAP Food Benefit on the customer-facing screen.
If cash back is turned on, ask about cash back for an EBT Cash Benefit Card.
Ask the customer to enter their EBT PIN, then tap Enter.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: On the customer-facing screen, request that the customer select Cash Benefit or SNAP Food Benefit.

entries.title: Take an EBT payment in the Sale app
steps: Open the Sale app.
Enter the transaction amount, then tap EBT.
On the customer-facing screen, tap Cash benefit or SNAP food benefit.
Insert or swipe the EBT card. For SNAP Food Benefit you can tap Manual card entry and enter the card number and expiration date.
Tap Continue.
If cash back is turned on, ask about cash back for an EBT Cash Benefit Card.
Ask the customer to enter their EBT PIN, then tap Enter.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: Enter the transaction amount, then tap EBT.

entries.title: Take an EBT payment in the Sale app by tapping Charge
steps: Open the Sale app.
Enter the transaction amount, then tap Charge.
Insert or swipe the EBT card.
On the customer-facing screen, tap Cash benefit or SNAP food benefit.
If cash back is turned on, ask about cash back for an EBT Cash Benefit Card.
Ask the customer to enter their EBT PIN, then tap Enter.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: Enter the transaction amount, then tap Charge.

entries.title: Cash back on an EBT payment
steps: Cash back is offered only if you have turned it on.
It applies to customers paying with an EBT Cash Benefit Card: ask whether they want cash back and how much.
entries.quote: ask customers paying with an EBT Cash Benefit Card to choose if they want cash back and how much they want.

entries.title: EBT card will not read: key it in (Register app)
steps: Manual entry works only for EBT SNAP Food Benefits. An EBT Cash card must be swiped or inserted.
Open the Register app, add items and tap Review Order.
Tap Pay.
Under Other, tap EBT.
Tap Cash Benefit or SNAP Food Benefit, then tap Pay.
On the Swipe EBT or SNAP Food Benefit Card screen, tap Type Card.
Enter the EBT card number, then tap Enter.
Enter the card expiry date, then tap Enter.
Ask the customer to enter their EBT PIN, then tap Enter.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: On the Swipe EBT or SNAP Food Benefit Card screen, tap Type Card.

entries.title: EBT card will not read: key it in (Sale app)
steps: Open the Sale app.
Enter the transaction amount.
Tap the option menu on the lower right, then tap EBT.
Tap Cash Benefit or SNAP Food Benefit, then tap Pay.
On the Swipe EBT or SNAP Food Benefit Card screen, tap Type Card.
Enter the EBT card number, then tap Enter.
Enter the expiry date, then tap Enter.
Ask the customer to enter the EBT PIN, then tap Enter.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: Tap the option menu on the lower right, and then tap EBT.

entries.title: EBT Cash card cannot be keyed in by hand
steps: Manual card entry is supported only for EBT SNAP Food Benefits.
An EBT Cash card must be swiped or inserted.
entries.quote: Manual entry card is only supported for EBT SNAP Food Benefits. EBT Cash card must be swiped or inserted to be accepted.

entries.title: Check an EBT card balance in the EBT app
steps: Open the EBT app.
Tap the benefit type: Cash Benefit or SNAP Food Benefit.
Tap Check Balance.
Swipe the EBT card.
The customer enters the EBT card PIN on the customer-facing screen, then tap Enter. The balance is displayed.
To print the balance, tap Print on the lower right corner of the Balance field.
entries.quote: The EBT app requires the EBT card PIN to check funds.

entries.title: Check the balance of an EBT card entered by hand (EBT app)
steps: Open the EBT app.
Tap the benefit type: Cash Benefit or SNAP Food Benefit.
Tap Check Balance.
Enter the card number, then tap Done.
Enter the card expiration date, then tap Done.
Ask the customer to enter the EBT card PIN, then tap Enter. The balance shows on the customer-facing screen.
To print it, tap Print on the lower right corner of the Balance field.
entries.quote: Enter the EBT card expiration date, then tap Done.

entries.title: Check an EBT balance while taking payment in the Register app
steps: Open the Register app.
Add items to the order, then select Pay.
In the Other section, tap EBT.
Tap Cash Benefit or SNAP Food Benefit.
Tap Check Balance.
Swipe the EBT card. For SNAP Food Benefit you can tap Manual Card Entry and enter the card number and expiration date.
Tap Continue.
The customer enters the EBT card PIN on the customer-facing screen, then tap Enter. The balance is displayed.
To print the balance, tap Print on the lower right corner of the Balance field.
entries.quote: Select Check Balance when taking an EBT or SNAP Food Benefit card payment with the Register or Sale app.

entries.title: Check an EBT balance in the Sale app
steps: Open the Sale app.
Enter the transaction amount, then select EBT.
On the customer-facing screen, tap Cash Benefit or SNAP Food Benefit.
Tap Check Balance.
Swipe the EBT card, or for SNAP Food Benefit tap Manual Card Entry.
Tap Continue.
The customer enters the EBT card PIN, then tap Enter. The balance is displayed.
To print the balance, tap Print on the lower right corner of the Balance field.
entries.quote: Enter the transaction amount, then select EBT.

entries.title: Refund an EBT payment (whole payment or chosen items)
steps: You need the Access transactions > Refund payments permission.
Open the Orders app.
Tap the EBT order you want to refund.
Tap Exchange/Refund.
Tap Refund Payment.
For a full refund tap the payment amount. For a partial refund select the items to refund.
Tap Refund and then confirm.
Swipe the EBT card or enter the card number by hand.
Ask the customer to enter their EBT PIN, then tap Enter.
entries.quote: For a full refund, tap the payment amount. For a partial refund, select the items you want to refund.

entries.title: Refund returned items on an EBT order
steps: Open the Orders app.
Find and open the customer order.
Select all items the customer wants to return.
Tap Refund.
Ask the customer to swipe their card or enter the card number by hand.
Ask the customer to enter their PIN, then select Enter.
Select Done.
entries.quote: Select all items the customer wants to return.

entries.title: Employee cannot refund an EBT payment
steps: The employee's role needs the Access transactions > Refund payments permission.
An owner or manager can change role permissions.
entries.quote: Note: To process refunds for EBT SNAP, you must have the Access transactions > Refund payments permission.

entries.title: Give a manual refund to a card in the Refund app
steps: You need the customer's payment card.
On the device, open the Refund app.
Enter a refund amount.
Tap Issue Refund and confirm.
If the device asks for an invoice number (or your custom identifier), enter it and tap Continue.
Swipe the customer's card, insert a chip card, tap for contactless, or enter the card number by hand.
entries.quote: Swipe the customer's payment card, insert a chip card, tap for contactless payment, or manually enter the card number.

entries.title: Refund a past transaction from the Refund app
steps: Open the Refund app.
Tap Look Up Past Payment.
Tap the transaction you want to refund.
Tap Refund.
Tap Refund in the pop-up.
Tap where to apply the refund.
entries.quote: Tap Look Up Past Payment.

entries.title: 'The unmatched refund limit was exceeded. Refund declined.'
steps: This means you have gone over your daily limit for manual refunds, which is based on the recent activity of your business.
You cannot process any more manual refunds that day.
Refunding a payment from the original order or transaction is a separate route: the source says to use the Orders app for refunding items on an order.
entries.quote: Note: If you have exceeded your daily limit for manual refunds, an error message appears: 'The unmatched refund limit was exceeded. Refund declined.'
entries.note: The source does not say how the limit can be raised.

entries.title: Daily limit on manual refunds
steps: There is a daily limit for manual refunds, based on the recent activity of your business.
Once you go over it in a single day, no more manual refunds can be processed that day.
entries.quote: There is a daily limit for manual refunds based on the recent activity of your business.

entries.title: Refund button is missing on transaction payments
steps: The Refund button appears only when two-factor authentication is enabled.
Set up two-factor authentication.
Also check your role has the Access manual transaction > Perform manual refund permission.
entries.quote: The Refund button appears in your transaction payments only when two-factor authentication is enabled.

entries.title: Tips are refunded with a manual refund
steps: You can manually refund part or all of the transaction amount.
If the refunded transaction includes tips, the tips are also refunded.
entries.quote: If the refunded transaction includes tips, the tips are also refunded.

entries.title: Refund app or Orders app
steps: Use the Refund app for manual refunds of recent and past transactions. They are recorded in the Transactions app.
Use the Orders app to refund individual items on an order or to exchange one item for another.
entries.quote: If you want to refund individual items on an order or exchange one item for another, use the Orders app instead.

entries.title: How long after a sale a refund can be made (dashboard article)
steps: Refunds should be issued as soon as possible.
Typically refunds can be processed for up to 120 days after the transaction.
A refund goes back to the original form of payment.
Some processing fees may apply; policies vary by processor agreement.
entries.quote: Typically, refunds can be processed for up to 120 days after the transaction.
entries.note: Fee and policy questions go to client services.

entries.title: Refund a payment on the dashboard and choose whether to refund the tip
steps: Two-factor authentication must be on and you need the Refund payments permission.
Log in to your Clover dashboard.
From the left, select Sales Activity > Transactions.
Select Payments.
Find the payment and select Details.
Select Issue Refund.
Enter the amount to refund, up to the maximum shown.
Decide whether to refund the tip.
Select Refund and then Confirm Refund.
Review the refund under Transactions > Refunds.
entries.quote: (Optional) Decide if you want to refund the tip.

entries.title: Make staff give a reason for every void and refund
steps: Log in to your Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Transactions, select Payments.
Under Track reasons, select the Voids and Refunds checkbox.
Use the default list of reasons, or delete ones you do not need with the trash icon.
Select Add a reason to add your own.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Under Track reasons, select the Voids and Refunds checkbox to enable tracking.

entries.title: Device asks for a reason when voiding or refunding
steps: This appears when reason tracking for voids and refunds is turned on.
Select a reason to continue.
The reason is saved in the details of the order or transaction and in the Transactions report.
entries.quote: they will be prompted to select a reason for their action.

entries.title: Reprint a receipt or send it again by email or text
steps: On the device, open the Transactions app.
Find the transaction.
Tap Receipts.
Select the way you want to reissue the receipt.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: You can reprint a receipt or reissue a receipt to the customer through email or text message.

entries.title: Find a transaction by scanning the customer receipt
steps: On the device, open the Transactions app.
On a Clover Flex, hold down the scanner button on the left side. On other Clover devices, tap the barcode icon in the lower left corner of the screen.
Position the receipt and let the camera scan it.
View the receipt record in the Transactions app.
entries.quote: On a Clover Flex, hold down the scanner button on the left side.

entries.title: Print a void receipt in the kitchen when items are voided (device)
steps: Open the Setup app.
Select Order Receipts & Sticky Labels > Order receipts.
Select the Void receipts checkbox to turn the setting on.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Select the Void receipts checkbox to turn on the setting.

entries.title: Turn kitchen void receipts on or off from the dashboard
steps: Log in to your Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Transactions, select Order receipts.
Under Void receipts, select Edit. The default setting is on.
Select or clear the 'Print void receipt for items that have been voided' checkbox.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Select or clear the 'Print void receipt for items that have been voided' checkbox, as needed.

entries.title: Set all unentered tips to zero at once
steps: On the device, open the Tips app.
Tap Autofill $0.00 tips.
Tap OK in the dialog box to confirm.
entries.quote: If you have one or more transactions with unentered tips, you can automatically set tips to zero for these transactions.

entries.title: Tips show in the Tips app but cannot be changed
steps: This happens when the device is set to take tips on the tablet screen: you see the tips in the Tips app but cannot adjust them.
When the device is set to take tips on printed receipts, select the transaction in the Tips app to enter the tip amount.
entries.quote: If you set your Clover device to accept tips on the tablet screen, you’ll see the tips in the Tips app, but you can’t adjust them.

entries.title: See which transactions still need a tip entered
steps: Open the Tips app.
Select Unentered to see transactions with unentered tips.
Select All to switch back to all transactions.
entries.quote: Select Unentered to see transactions with unentered tips.

entries.title: See transactions with unentered tips on the dashboard
steps: Log in to your Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Tips.
Select Filter By Enter or Unentered and then select Unentered Tips.
entries.quote: Select Filter By Enter or Unentered and then select Unentered Tips.

entries.title: Change the tip suggestions shown at checkout (device)
steps: You need the Access Tips > Set tips for all employees permission.
Open the Setup app.
Tap Tips > Tip suggestions.
Choose Tip percentages or Smart tipping.
Enter the percentages to use. You can enter up to 4 default tip suggestions.
Optionally enter a label for each tip amount.
Select the checkbox for each tip amount to show to the cardholder.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Tap Tips > Tip suggestions.

entries.title: Change the tip suggestions shown at checkout (dashboard)
steps: Log in to your Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Tips.
Select the Ask for tip checkbox.
Choose Tip percentages or Smart tipping.
Enter up to 4 default tip suggestions.
Optionally enter tip labels.
Select the checkbox for each tip amount to show.
Decide whether to include or exclude the tip from the tax calculation.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Decide to include or exclude the tip from the tax calculation.

entries.title: Show flat dollar tips on small sales (smart tipping)
steps: Open the Setup app and tap Tips > Tip suggestions.
Select the checkbox next to Enable smart tipping.
Enter an amount next to 'Use flat tipping for amounts up to'. Sales below it use flat tips; sales above it use percentages.
Enter the percentages and the flat tip amounts, up to 4 of each.
Tap Save.
To make all tips flat, set the threshold higher than your average check total.
entries.quote: You can ensure all tips are flat by setting the transaction amount threshold higher than your average check total.

entries.title: How many tip options can be shown
steps: You can set up to 4 default tip suggestions for a customer to choose from during checkout.
Tip options are a percentage of the total sale or a flat rate.
entries.quote: You can set up to 4 default tip suggestions for a customer to choose from during checkout.

entries.title: Turn on pre-auths and set the pre-auth amount
steps: Only owners and managers with the right permissions can do this.
On the device, open the Setup app.
Tap Payments.
Tap the Enable pre-auth checkbox.
Enter the maximum pre-auth amount, up to $5,000.00.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Enter the maximum pre-auth amount (up to $5,000.00) for bar tabs and other orders.

entries.title: Default and maximum pre-auth amount
steps: The default pre-auth amount is $25.
It can be raised up to a maximum of $5,000.
You can change it at any time in Setup > Payments.
entries.quote: The default pre-auth amount is $25 and can be adjusted up to a maximum of $5000.

entries.title: A pre-auth is declined
steps: A pre-auth may be declined if the customer's card does not have enough available funds for the pre-auth amount you have set.
The customer can use another card or payment method.
entries.quote: A pre-auth may be declined if the customer’s card does not have enough available funds for the set amount.
entries.note: Second step is drawn from the Dining pre-auth article, which says another payment method can be used for the final payment.

entries.title: Start a pre-auth for a table in the Dining app
steps: Pre-auths must be enabled in the Setup app first.
On the device, open the Dining app.
Select the table.
Tap More at the bottom left.
Tap Add Pre-auth.
Swipe or insert the card.
entries.quote: Enable pre-auths and set the pre-auth amount in the Setup app before creating a pre-auth.

entries.title: Start a bar tab with a pre-auth in the Dining app
steps: On the device, open the Dining app.
Swipe or insert the card.
A new Bar & More order appears with the customer's name and the pre-auth.
entries.quote: Swipe or insert the card. A new Bar & More order appears with the customer’s name and the pre-auth.

entries.title: Void a pre-auth in the Dining app
steps: On the device, open the Dining app.
Select the table or Bar & More order.
Tap More at the bottom left.
Tap Void Pre-auth, then tap to confirm.
This only removes the hold on the card. It does not delete the order.
entries.quote: Tap Void Pre-auth, then tap to confirm.

entries.title: Final payment does not have to be on the pre-auth card
steps: The card used for the pre-auth does not have to be used for the final payment.
The customer can pay with another payment method.
entries.quote: The card used for the pre-auth does not have to be used for the final payment.

entries.title: Employee cannot void a pre-auth
steps: By default only Admins and Managers can void pre-auths.
Other employees need the Access Authorizations > Void authorizations permission added to their role.
entries.quote: By default, only Admins and Managers can void pre-auths.

entries.title: Completing a pre-auth for more than the original amount: Clover recommendation
steps: On the dashboard an authorization can be completed for less, or for up to 200% more than the original amount.
To reduce the risk of large chargebacks, Clover recommends not going over 120% of the original authorization amount.
entries.quote: To prevent the risk of large chargebacks, Clover recommends that you do not exceed 120% of the original authorization amount.

entries.title: Void a pre-auth in the Register app
steps: On the device, open the Register app.
Select the order.
Select More at the bottom left.
Select Void pre-auth.
entries.quote: By default, Admins and managers can void pre-auths. To void pre-auths, employees must have the Register > Void pre-authorization permission.

entries.title: Cardholder name shows as an order note after a pre-auth
steps: When you create a pre-auth in the Register app, the cardholder name appears as an order note.
You can edit the cardholder name.
entries.quote: If you create a pre-auth in the Register app, the cardholder name will appear as an order note.

entries.title: Add a note to an order in the Register app
steps: Open the Register app and add items.
Next to the name of the order at the top left, select the More menu and select Add Note.
Enter your note.
Select Save. The note shows just below the order name.
entries.quote: Next to the name of the order at the top left, select the More menu, and select Add Note.

entries.title: No Add Note option in the Register app
steps: A manager may need to turn it on.
In the Register app, swipe from the left to open Settings.
Select the Enable order notes checkbox.
To show order notes on order receipts, go to Setup app > Order Receipts and select Order Note.
entries.quote: Your manager can go to Register app Settings (swipe from the left in the Register app) and select the Enable order notes checkbox.

entries.title: Reopen a closed (paid) order
steps: On the device, open the Orders app.
Select the order you want to reopen.
On the right, select Reopen order.
The payments are voided and the order reopens.
entries.quote: On the right, select Reopen order. Payment(s) are voided, and the order will reopen.

entries.title: No Reopen order button
steps: If you do not see Reopen order, the order cannot be reopened.
Only orders that can still be voided can be reopened.
Orders with tips on paper can be reopened until closeout.
Orders with tips entered on the device can be reopened for up to 25 minutes after the order is taken.
entries.quote: For orders with tips entered on the device, reopening is allowed for up to 25 minutes after the order is taken.

entries.title: Add an item to an order by searching
steps: Open the Register app.
In the Scan barcode or search field, enter the item name, SKU or product code.
Tap the item in the search results.
If more than one, select the quantity on the QTY bar at the top.
Tap Add.
entries.quote: In the Scan barcode or search field, enter one of these—item name, SKU, or product code.

entries.title: Add an item by scanning its barcode with the device camera
steps: The barcode must already be saved against the item in your inventory.
Open the Register app.
Tap the barcode icon at the lower left. The camera switches on.
Hold the item in front of the camera and scan the barcode.
If more than one, select the quantity on the QTY bar.
Tap Add.
entries.quote: Tap the barcode icon at the lower left. The camera switches on, and you'll see the image it sees.

entries.title: Ring up something that is not in the inventory (custom item)
steps: Open the Register app.
Tap Add.
Use the number pad to set a price.
Next to Quantity, tap the number and set the quantity.
Next to Item Name, tap Edit and name the item.
To charge your default tax rate, select the Apply Default Taxes checkbox.
To keep the item for next time, select the Add to Inventory checkbox.
Tap Add item, or Add & Create Another.
entries.quote: To apply your default tax rate to the custom item, select the Apply Default Taxes checkbox.

entries.title: No tax charged on a custom item
steps: Select the Apply Default Taxes checkbox when creating the custom item.
If no default tax rate is set up, the system charges no tax.
entries.quote: If you have no default tax rate set up, the system charges no tax.

entries.title: No Add button on the Register header on a Flex
steps: The Add button on the screen header is not available on the Clover Flex.
Use Custom Item in the More menu at the upper right, or Custom Item as the last item in each category.
entries.quote: Tap Add on the screen header. (This is not available on the Clover Flex.)

entries.title: Custom items do not print at the kitchen (order) printer
steps: A manager goes to the Setup app > Order Receipts > Order receipt print timing.
Choose 'Print when hitting Pay' to print all items including custom items.
Or choose 'Fire when hitting Pay' or 'Fire when hitting Save' and also select the 'Print manually instead of firing if an item does not have a printer label' checkbox.
entries.quote: Print when hitting Pay—Prints all items, including custom items, in the order.

entries.title: Sell an item priced by weight
steps: You need a weight scale attached to the device.
Open the Register app.
Select the item priced by weight.
Place the item on the scale.
To subtract the container's weight, tap Set Tare and enter the tare weight.
Tap Add.
entries.quote: To subtract the weight of the container holding the item, tap Set Tare and enter the tare weight on the number pad.

entries.title: Tare weight cannot be changed after the item is added
steps: After a priced per-unit item is added to an order, the tare weight cannot be edited.
Check the numbers before you tap Add.
entries.quote: Note: After adding a priced per-unit item to an order, you won’t be able to edit the tare weight.

entries.title: Change the quantity of an item on an order
steps: After adding the item, tap its name in the Order section and use the Minus or Plus buttons, or tap the quantity number to bring up a keypad. Tap Done.
Or, on all devices except Clover Flex, use the QTY bar at the top of the screen.
You may need permission to change a quantity to zero.
entries.quote: After adding an item to the order, tap the item name in the Order section and use the Minus or Plus buttons.

entries.title: QTY bar is not showing in the Register app
steps: On the Register homepage, tap Menu at the top left.
Select Settings.
Select 'Enable quantity (QTY) bar on items screen'.
This setting is per device. The QTY bar is not on the Clover Flex.
entries.quote: Not seeing the QTY bar? On the Register homepage, tap Menu at the top left, select Settings, and select the 'Enable quantity (QTY) bar on items screen'.

entries.title: Change the preset numbers on the QTY bar
steps: Tap and hold a preset number (any except 1), then enter a new number.
Changes apply only to this device.
entries.quote: You can change any of the preset numbers except 1 by tapping and holding the number, then entering a new preset number.

entries.title: Pop-up asking to confirm the customer age
steps: It appears when an age-restricted item, such as alcohol, is added to an order.
The employee confirms the customer's age.
Once confirmed the item is added and checkout continues.
entries.quote: If the item is age-restricted, a pop-up appears. The employee needs to confirm the customer’s age.

entries.title: Add modifiers to an item on an order
steps: In the Register app, add items to the order.
Select the item that has a modifier group.
Select the modifiers you want.
To add more of a modifier, tap the number on the right side of the modifier button. To reduce it, tap the minus button on the left.
To remove a modifier, tap the center of the modifier button.
Select Done.
entries.quote: To remove the modifier from the item, tap the center of the modifier button.

entries.title: Change the modifiers on an item already in the order
steps: In your order in the Register app, select the item.
Select Modifiers to open the modifier selection screen.
Edit the modifiers.
Select Done.
entries.quote: Select Modifiers to open the modifier selection screen.

entries.title: Add a one-off instruction to an item (custom modifier)
steps: In the Register app, add the item to the order.
Tap the item in the Orders sidebar.
Tap the Custom modifier field and enter the custom modifier name, for example No Nuts.
Tap Done. The new modifier shows under the item in the Orders sidebar.
entries.quote: Tap the Custom modifier field and enter the custom modifier name.

entries.title: Open and change Register app settings
steps: On the device, open the Register app.
Tap the Menu icon at the upper left.
Tap Settings.
Use the checkboxes to switch settings on and off.
Managers can tap See Additional Settings to reach more settings in the Setup app.
entries.quote: Managers can also tap See Additional Settings to find additional settings in the Setup app.

entries.title: Register jumps back to the home screen after every item
steps: Open Register app Settings.
Select 'Remain in category after adding an item to an order'.
entries.quote: If this is not selected, adding an item returns you to the Register app home screen.

entries.title: Identical items show on separate lines or grouped
steps: Register app Settings has 'Group identical items into one line'.
Identical items with different modifiers are not grouped together.
entries.quote: Identical items that don’t have the same modifiers chosen will not be grouped together.

entries.title: Only one modifier group shows at a time
steps: Open Register app Settings.
Select 'View all modifier groups at a time' to show all modifier groups on one scrollable screen.
entries.quote: If this is not selected, you can only view one modifier group at a time.

entries.title: Take the tax off one order
steps: On the device, open the Register app.
In the left panel, next to the order type, select Options > Remove Taxes.
To put the tax back, select Options > Add Taxes.
entries.quote: In the left panel, next to the order type, select Options > Remove Taxes.

entries.title: No Remove Taxes option on an order
steps: A manager with permission logs in on the device.
Open the Register app.
Swipe in from the left on the Register screen and tap Settings.
Select the 'Enable manual removal of taxes and fees' checkbox.
entries.quote: Select the 'Enable manual removal of taxes and fees' checkbox.
entries.note: Another Clover article names this checkbox 'Allow taxes to be removed from an order'.

entries.title: Turn on 'Allow taxes to be removed from an order'
steps: In the Register app, tap Menu in the upper left, then tap Settings.
Select the 'Allow taxes to be removed from an order' checkbox.
During a sale, tap Options next to the order type, then tap Remove Taxes.
To undo, tap Add Taxes.
entries.quote: To remove taxes from an order, in the Register app settings, select the 'Allow taxes to be removed from an order' checkbox.
entries.note: Another Clover article names this checkbox 'Enable manual removal of taxes and fees'.

entries.title: Discount one item on an order
steps: You need the Access Register > Apply custom discounts or Apply Discounts to items permission.
Open the Register app and add the items.
Select the item in the Orders sidebar.
Tap Add Discount.
Select the discount.
For Custom Percentage Discount or Custom Amount Discount, enter it on the number pad and tap Apply.
Tap Done.
To remove a discount, tap Delete next to it.
entries.quote: To remove a discount, tap Delete next to the discount.

entries.title: Discount a whole order
steps: Open the Register app and add items to the order.
Select Options > Order Discounts.
Select Add Discount.
Select a discount option.
For a custom percentage or amount, enter it on the number pad.
Tap Apply.
To remove it, tap Remove next to the discount.
entries.quote: Select Options > Order Discounts.

entries.title: Item discounts and an order discount on the same order
steps: You can apply several discounts to an order.
When there are both item discounts and an order discount, the item discounts are applied first.
entries.quote: If you apply both discounts to items and a discount to the entire order, the system applies the item discounts first.

entries.title: Employee cannot apply a discount
steps: The role needs the Access Register > Apply custom discounts or Apply Discounts to items permission.
entries.quote: Note: To apply discounts, you must have the Access Register > Apply custom discounts or Apply Discounts to items permission.

entries.title: Add a service charge to an order in the Register app
steps: The service charge must already be set up in the Setup app or on the dashboard.
Create the order in the Register app.
After adding the items, select Options on the left side, above the order.
Select the checkbox next to each service charge to apply.
Tap Save. The service charge shows in the subtotal.
entries.quote: After you add all the order items, select Options on the left side, above the order.

entries.title: Add a service charge to a table in the Dining app
steps: On the device, open the Dining app.
Tap the table.
Tap Options at the bottom, next to Pay.
Tap Edit Service Charge.
Select the checkboxes for the service charges to apply.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Tap Edit Service Charge.

entries.title: Set up a service charge on the dashboard
steps: Log in to your Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Additional charges.
Select Edit.
Select the 'Enable service charges' checkbox and select Save.
Select Add service charge and enter its name and percentage.
Optionally turn on 'Allow removing fees' so employees can remove it from an order.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Select the 'Enable service charges' checkbox and then select Save.

entries.title: Service charge limits
steps: Up to eight service charges can be added.
Only one service charge can be set as auto-gratuity at a time.
An auto-gratuity service charge applies automatically once the guest threshold is reached.
entries.quote: Only one service charge can be assigned as auto-gratuity at a time.

entries.title: Change the order type on an order (for example to-go to dine-in)
steps: In the Register app, add items to the order.
In the Orders sidebar, next to the current order type, select the More menu and choose Edit Order Type.
Select a different order type.
entries.quote: In the Orders sidebar, next to the current order type listed, select the More menu and choose Edit Order Type.

entries.title: Change how items are laid out in the Register app
steps: On the device, open the Register app.
Tap the More menu at the upper right.
Tap Register Display.
Select the display you want: Categories & Items view, Category view or List View.
Tap X at the upper left when done.
entries.quote: You can adjust the way items are displayed on your device screen when you use the Register app.

entries.title: Cannot switch the Register to category view
steps: If the inventory has 10,000 or more items, only list view is available.
entries.quote: If your inventory has 10,000 or more items, only list view is available and you can't switch to category view.

entries.title: Attach a customer to an order in the Register app
steps: Start the order in the Register app and add items.
In the left panel, select the More menu and choose Add Customer.
In the Customers app, find and select the customer.
The customer's name is added in the order note area just above the items.
entries.quote: In the left panel, select the More menu and choose Add Customer.

entries.title: Take payment with a Clover gift card
steps: On the device, open the Register or Sales app.
On the Payments screen, select Other.
Select Gift cards.
Swipe: tap Charge and swipe the card. Manual entry: tap Gift/Card manual and enter the card number. QR code: tap Gift/Scan QR code and scan the code on the customer's phone or printed copy.
When the payment completes, print a gift card receipt. It shows the new balance if any is left.
entries.quote: Manual entry: Tap Gift/Card manual and enter the card number.

entries.title: Check a gift card balance
steps: On the device, open the Gift cards app.
Tap Check card balance.
Enter the gift card number or scan the gift card QR code.
Review the balance and history on the screen.
Tap Print Balance to print it for the customer.
Tap Done.
entries.quote: Review the balance and history on the screen.

entries.title: Add money to (reload) a gift card
steps: On the device, open the Gift cards app.
Tap Add money.
Enter the gift card number or scan the gift card QR code.
Tap a preset amount or tap Custom.
Tap Continue.
Tap Add to order to add it to an existing Register order, or tap Take payment and complete the payment.
Once payment is processed, tap Done.
Optionally tap Print receipt so the customer has a record of the new balance.
entries.quote: Tap a predefined amount or tap Custom to enter a specific amount to load the gift card.

entries.title: Cash out the remaining balance on a gift card
steps: On the device, open the Gift cards app.
Tap Cash out.
Enter the gift card number or scan the gift card QR code.
Review the balance and tap Cash out.
Tap Confirm to zero out the card.
Tap OK and give the cash from your drawer.
entries.quote: Tap Confirm to zero out the card.

entries.title: Card inactive (gift card)
steps: This message appears when you try to use a gift card that has been cashed out.
You can add money to the gift card if needed.
entries.quote: If you try to use the gift card, the Card inactive message appears. You can add money to the gift card if needed.

entries.title: Sell a plastic gift card from the Gift cards app
steps: On the device, open the Gift cards app.
Select Sell gift cards.
Under Card type, tap Plastic.
Enter or select a quantity.
Tap a preset amount or Custom, then select Continue.
Swipe the card, scan its barcode or enter the card number by hand. Repeat for each card.
Tap Continue.
Review the total, then tap Add to order or Take payment.
Once payment is processed, tap Done.
entries.quote: Swipe or scan the barcode, or enter the card number manually.

entries.title: Sell a plastic gift card from the Register app
steps: On the device, open the Register app.
Select Gift card from the inventory items.
Enter the amount and select Add.
In the Gift cards app, select Plastic.
Swipe the gift card, scan the barcode or enter the number to activate it.
Take the payment on the Register Payment screen. A gift card receipt prints automatically.
entries.quote: Swipe the gift card, scan the barcode, or manually enter the gift card number to activate the gift card.

entries.title: Plastic gift cards: per-sale limit and fee
steps: Up to 20 plastic gift cards of the same value can be issued in a single transaction.
Clover says a 2.5% fee may be charged on the total amount of the gift cards. Fee questions go to client services.
entries.quote: You can issue up to 20 physical gift cards of the same value in a single transaction.

entries.title: Sell a digital gift card from the device
steps: On the device, open the Gift cards app.
Select Sell a gift card.
Under Card type, select Digital gift card.
Enter a quantity (up to 10 in one order).
Enter the amount, then select Continue.
Choose Email or Text, enter the recipient's email address or mobile number, and select Continue.
Review, then tap Add to order or Take payment.
Follow the prompts and tap Done. A digital gift card receipt prints automatically.
entries.quote: Enter or select a quantity. You can select up to 10 for a single order.

entries.title: Gift cards not working yet after signing up
steps: After you accept the terms in the Gift cards app, full activation for selling and using gift cards on the device can take up to 24 hours.
entries.quote: Full gift card program activation for selling/using gift cards on your Clover device can still take up to 24 hours.

entries.title: Give store credit on a gift card instead of a refund
steps: On the device, open the Gift cards app.
Tap Issue store credit.
Select a reason, for example complimentary credit, refund or donation.
Under Card type choose Plastic or Digital.
Tap a preset amount or Custom, then select Continue.
Plastic card: swipe, scan the barcode or enter the number. Digital: enter the customer's email or mobile number.
Review the summary.
Tap Take payment, then tap Charge $0.00 on card and tap Done.
Tap Print receipt so the customer has a record of the balance.
entries.quote: Tap Charge $0.00 on card and tap Done.

entries.title: Let employees add money to, cash out or load gift cards
steps: On the device, open the Employees app.
Select Permissions.
Select Gift Cards.
Tick the permission for the employee role: Add money to gift card, Cash out gift card, or Load gift card without a payment.
entries.quote: Cash out gift card: Employees can convert a gift card to cash value.

entries.title: Take payment from one guest at a table (Dining app)
steps: Open Clover Dining.
Select the table.
At the bottom of the order, select the arrow to the right of Pay.
Select Pay by guest.
If there are Whole table items, you are prompted to split their cost evenly among guests.
Select the guest and select Next.
The order stays open until all payments are completed.
entries.quote: You can take payment from a single guest without charging the rest of the table. The order will remain open until all payments are completed.

entries.title: Cannot apply a dollar discount when one guest pays
steps: When taking payment from a single guest you can apply a percentage discount but not a dollar amount discount.
entries.quote: Keep in mind that when you take a payment from a single guest, you can apply a percentage discount but not a dollar amount discount.

entries.title: Split the cost of an item among guests at a table
steps: Open Clover Dining.
Select the table.
Next to Whole Table, select More.
Select Split Item Cost.
On the left, tap the item or items to split.
Select the guests who are splitting them.
Select Confirm.
If a guest will leave early, split the item before printing that guest's bill.
entries.quote: You can split the cost of an item evenly among all the guests at a table.

entries.title: Print the bill for a whole table
steps: Open Clover Dining.
Select the table and add items to the order.
Select More at the lower left and choose Print Entire Bill.
entries.quote: Select More at the lower left and choose Print Entire Bill.

entries.title: Print a bill for one guest
steps: Open Clover Dining.
Select the table.
Next to the guest number, select More and choose Print Bill.
The guest must have ordered at least one item.
entries.quote: Next to the guest number, select More, and choose Print Bill.

entries.title: Print separate bills for every guest at once
steps: Open the Clover Dining app.
Tap the table.
At the lower left, tap More and choose Print Individual Bills.
Items ordered for the whole table are split evenly across the individual bills.
entries.quote: At the lower left, tap More and choose Print Individual Bills.

entries.title: How guests pay with the QR code on the bill (Scan to Pay)
steps: Scan to Pay is on automatically on devices running the Dining app. A QR code prints at the bottom of each table-level bill.
The guest scans the QR code with their phone camera and a secure payment link opens.
The guest picks a payment method: Apple Pay on iOS, Google Pay on Android, or manual card entry on a Clover-hosted page.
The guest chooses a tip.
The guest reviews the total and taps Pay.
entries.quote: When enabled, a unique QR code is printed at the bottom of each table-level printed bill

entries.title: No Scan to Pay QR code on a printed bill
steps: QR codes do not print on bills for individual guests or split bills.
Print one bill for the whole table to get the QR code.
entries.quote: Note: Scan to Pay QR codes do not appear on bills for individual guests or split bills.

entries.title: Stop the Scan to Pay QR code printing on bills
steps: On the device: open the Setup app and tap Payments, then clear the Enable Scan to Pay checkbox.
Or on the dashboard: Settings > View all settings, under Transactions select Payments, and in Scan to Pay Settings clear the Enable Scan to Pay checkbox.
entries.quote: Clear the Enable Scan to Pay checkbox.

entries.title: Combine two orders so one person can pay
steps: You need the Access Register > Combine Orders permission.
On the device, open the Dining app.
Open the order you want to combine with another.
Select More at the bottom left.
Select Combine Orders.
Select the table or Bar & More order to combine with.
Select Confirm.
entries.quote: Select the table or Bar & More order you want to combine with.

entries.title: Orders will not combine: one has a pre-auth
steps: Orders containing pre-auths cannot be combined.
Void any pre-auths in the Orders app first, then combine the orders.
entries.quote: Orders containing pre-auths can’t be combined; be sure to void any pre-auths in the Orders app before combining orders.

entries.title: Two or duplicate orders on the same table
steps: This can happen when a device was offline when the order was taken, when several servers are assigned to the table, or from a system issue.
Make sure the device is online.
On the Dining floor plan, select the table to open the side panel. It lists the orders and their times.
Tap an order to review or edit it.
If the items are all correct but were taken at different times, select Combine orders at the bottom of the panel.
If an order belongs to another table, select Move order.
To delete an order, tap it to edit, clear the order and close it.
entries.quote: Multiple or duplicated orders may be taken for the same table in Clover Dining.

entries.title: Preventing duplicate table orders
steps: Make sure all devices are online before taking orders.
Assign only one server to a table at a time.
entries.quote: In order to prevent multiple orders from occurring, ensure that all devices are online prior to taking the order(s).

entries.title: Delete an open table order
steps: You need the Access Register > Delete Open Orders permission.
On the device, open the Dining app.
Select the table.
Select More at the bottom left.
Select Delete.
The order must contain at least one item to be deleted.
entries.quote: An order must contain at least one item to be deleted.

entries.title: Delete an open Bar & More (non-table) order
steps: You need the Access Register > Delete Open Orders permission.
Open the Dining app.
Tap Bar & More.
Tap the order.
Tap More on the lower left.
Tap Delete Order.
Tap Delete.
entries.quote: All non-table orders are located in the Bar & More section.

entries.title: Hand a table over to another server
steps: Open Clover Dining.
Select the table.
Select More at the bottom left.
Select Transfer Server.
Select the server and tap Transfer.
entries.quote: Select Transfer Server.

entries.title: Move an order to another table
steps: Open Clover Dining.
Select the table.
Select More at the bottom left.
Select Move Order.
Select An Available Table, or Bar & More to make it a non-table order.
Select the table and select Confirm.
To undo, tap UNDO in the message at the bottom of the screen.
entries.quote: Select An Available Table to move the order to a new table, or Bar & More to make the order a floating (non-table) order.

entries.title: Move one guest and their tab to another table
steps: Open Clover Dining.
Select the table where the guest is seated.
Select More next to the guest.
Select Move Guest.
Choose another table or Bar & More.
Select the table or bill to move the guest to.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Select the option to move the guest to another table or to Bar & More.

entries.title: Move items from one guest to another
steps: Open Clover Dining.
Select the table.
Tap More next to Whole Table or the guest who has the items.
Tap Move Items.
Select the items, then select the guest to move them to.
entries.quote: Select the items you want to move; then select the guest to move items to.

entries.title: Send items to the kitchen printer one at a time
steps: On the device, open the Dining app.
Select the table.
Tap More.
Tap Refire to Kitchen.
Tick the items to fire, then tap Print.
Repeat until all items are fired.
entries.quote: Select the checkboxes for the item(s) you want to fire, then tap Print.

entries.title: Whole order went to the kitchen when only some items were meant to
steps: Tapping Fire or Pay fires all items in the order.
To go back to the floor plan before every item is fired, tap the Back button at the top left instead.
entries.quote: Tapping Fire or Pay fires all items in the order.

entries.title: Send a table order to the kitchen printer
steps: Open Clover Dining.
Select a table containing an order.
Select Fire.
Each item sent shows the word Printed on the Dining sidebar.
entries.quote: In addition, every item on the order receipt displays the word Printed on the Clover Dining sidebar.

entries.title: Find an open takeout or bar order
steps: On the device, open Clover Dining.
Select Bar & More.
Select Search and enter a customer name, order ID, order number, order note or last 4 digits of the payment card.
Select the order.
entries.quote: To find any open non-table order, use the search bar in the Bar & More section.

entries.title: Take a takeout, delivery, curbside or bar order in the Dining app
steps: On the device, open the Clover Dining app.
Tap Bar & More.
Select an order type: Takeout, Delivery, Curbside pickup or Bar.
Tap Add.
Optionally select the number of guests and tap Save.
Add items and tap Done.
Tap Pay to take payment.
entries.quote: Tap Bar & More to create a non-table order.

entries.title: Wrong order type picked on a non-table order
steps: The order may show incorrectly in reports or workflows.
If possible, update the order type before completing payment.
entries.quote: The order may appear incorrectly in reports or workflows. If possible, update the order type before completing payment.

entries.title: Take an order for a table in the Dining app
steps: On the device, open the Dining app.
On the floor plan, select a table.
Tap Whole Table to add items for everyone, or tap a guest number to add items for one guest.
Add items. The Dining app shows items that are assigned to a category.
For an item not in a category, type its name in the search field.
entries.quote: To add items for the entire table, tap Whole Table.

entries.title: An item does not show in the Dining app
steps: The Dining app displays items that are assigned to a category.
Enter the item name in the search field to find an item that is not in a category.
entries.quote: (Optional) To add an item that isn’t assigned to a category, enter the item name in the search field to find it.

entries.title: Guest rows have disappeared from a table order
steps: The guest list is collapsed, which only hides guest details. It does not remove or merge guest orders.
Tap the chevron icon next to Guests to expand the view.
entries.quote: It does not remove or merge guest orders. All guest details reappear when you expand the view.

entries.title: Open Clover Dining settings
steps: On the device, open the Dining app.
Select Menu at the upper left.
Select Settings.
entries.quote: Clover Dining settings let you control the way orders are taken and set up the Fast Action Bar for frequently used actions.

entries.title: Why a table turns red on the floor plan
steps: Tables display as red an hour and a half after the order is opened.
The time can be changed in Dining settings under 'Mark tables in red'.
entries.quote: Mark tables in red: Tables display as red an hour and a half after opening the order.

entries.title: Order receipts do not print at the kitchen printer automatically
steps: By default the system does not automatically print order receipts.
Open the Setup app.
Tap Order receipts.
Tap 'How will order receipts be printed in Register?'.
Under Auto printing, choose All items or Only items with printer labels.
Under When to print, choose Pay or Save, Pay, Save, or Customer receipts are printed.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: By default, the system doesn't automatically print order receipts to the connected order printer.

entries.title: Print order receipts by hand with the printer icon
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Order receipts.
Tap 'How would you like receipts to be printed in Register?'.
Under Manual printing, select 'Tap printer icon to print manually'.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Under Manual printing, select 'Tap printer icon to print manually'.

entries.title: Require a manager passcode to reprint an order receipt
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Order receipts.
Select the 'Reprinting order receipt requires manager passcode' checkbox.
entries.quote: Select the 'Reprinting order receipt requires manager passcode' checkbox.

entries.title: Device asks for a manager passcode when reprinting an order receipt
steps: This is a setting that stops employees printing multiple order receipts.
A manager enters their passcode, or the setting can be cleared in the Setup app under Order receipts.
entries.quote: You can prevent employees from printing multiple order receipts by requiring a manager's passcode to reprint receipts.

entries.title: Choose which items print at which order printer
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Order receipts.
Tap Order receipt printer to see the list of printers.
If your printer is not listed, select + to add it.
Select a printer.
Select the labels to print to this printer.
Tap Save.
If several printers have the same label, the item prints on all of them.
entries.quote: If multiple printers have the same printer label, the item prints on all designated printers.

entries.title: Put order numbers on receipts
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Order receipts.
Tap Order numbers.
Choose None, Automatic or Manual.
Tap Save.
This setting is per device, so repeat it on other Clover devices.
entries.quote: This setting is device-specific, so you’ll need to change this on other Clover devices if you want them to work the same way.

entries.title: Make order receipts shorter
steps: Open the Setup app.
Tap Order receipts.
Under Customize order receipts, select Edit.
Choose to group similar items, consolidate line items across guests, or condense modifiers.
Select Save.
entries.quote: You can shorten order receipts by consolidating similar items and orders.

entries.title: Send Kiosk orders to a kitchen printer
steps: If in kiosk mode, long-press the Clover logo in the bottom left corner, then in Admin settings select Exit kiosk mode.
From the home screen, open the Printers app.
Tap the plus icon in the bottom-right corner.
Select Order Printer and pick the printer found on the network. Do not print orders to the Kiosk printer.
Tap the printer to open its settings.
Rename it, print a test receipt and assign printer labels.
entries.quote: Select Order Printer. (Note: Do not print orders to the Kiosk printer.)

entries.title: Kiosk: send every order to one kitchen printer
steps: After adding the printer, open the Setup app.
Select Order Receipts.
Select 'How will order receipts be printed in Register?'.
Under Auto printing > What to print, select All items.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Under Auto printing > What to print, select All items.

entries.title: Show Kiosk orders on a Kitchen Display
steps: On the Clover KDS, select Settings in the upper left corner.
Make sure Kitchen mode is selected.
Assign all printer labels you want shown on that KDS. Changes save automatically.
Repeat on each Kitchen Display.
entries.quote: Make sure that Kitchen mode is selected and assign all printer labels that you would like shown on that KDS.

entries.title: Print a barcode on order receipts to pull up the order by scanning
steps: In the Setup app, select Order Receipts.
Under Customize order receipts, select Edit.
Make sure Show barcode is selected.
Select Save.
Scan the barcode with the Clover device to pull up the order.
entries.quote: Scan the barcode with your Clover device to quickly pull up the related order.

entries.title: How customers scan items at the Kiosk
steps: The customer starts an ordering session on the Kiosk.
They scan the item barcode with the scanner.
A success chime plays, a confirmation shows the item name and price, and the item goes into the cart.
They can still browse categories on screen and change quantities or remove items in the cart.
entries.quote: Confirmation message displays the item name, price, and basic attributes.

entries.title: Print a sales report from the device
steps: Open the Reporting app.
Select the type of report, such as Sales Overview, Employee Sales, Item Sales, Discount or Taxes.
Use the filters to adjust the date range or report type.
Tap the Print icon to send the report to your default printer.
entries.quote: Tap the Print icon to send the report to your default printer.

entries.title: Print a sales report or save it as a PDF from the dashboard
steps: Log in to your Clover dashboard.
Select Reports and open the report.
Use the filters to show what you want to print.
At the top right, select Print.
For a PDF, select Save as PDF. To print, choose a printer, select landscape layout and select Print.
entries.quote: If you’re printing the report, choose a printer, select landscape layout, and then select Print.

entries.title: Columns are missing from a report
steps: The report may be too wide for the device or printer, columns may be hidden or filtered out, or the device may not support full report formatting.
Check no filter (employee, device, tender type) is hiding data.
Add or remove columns in the report settings.
Try exporting the report to see all columns.
entries.quote: Some possible causes may be that your report is too wide for your device or printer to display fully

entries.title: Report is blank or will not load
steps: Adjust the date range to include known transactions.
Remove or reset filters.
Restart the Clover device.
Internet connection problems can also cause this.
entries.quote: Reports may appear blank if the date range is too narrow or too broad, no transactions match the selected filter, or if there are internet connectivity issues.

entries.title: Report totals look wrong or transactions are missing
steps: Double-check all filters: they may exclude certain employees, devices or payment types.
Remember that voided or refunded transactions affect totals.
Use the payments report to verify transactions.
Tap Sync and refresh the report.
entries.quote: Double-check all filters, use the payments report to verify transactions, or tap Sync and refresh the report.

entries.title: Wide reports do not fully show or print on a Flex or Mini
steps: Devices like the Flex or Mini may not fully display or print wide-format reports.
Use the dashboard on a computer for full report features, and print from a desktop browser.
entries.quote: Devices like the Flex or Mini may not fully display or print wide-format reports.

entries.title: Download a report
steps: Use the Download button in the upper-right corner of most reports.
Select a format: CSV, Excel or PDF.
For best results print from a desktop browser instead of a Clover device.
entries.quote: To export or print a report, use the Download button in the upper-right corner of most reports.

entries.title: Report shows a notice about declined payments
steps: This appears when payments taken while the system was offline were later declined. It shows the total of all declined payments.
Use the Transactions app to work with the declined payments.
entries.quote: If you accepted payments while the system was offline and any of those payments were declined, you’ll see a notice at the top of the report

entries.title: Report notes about partially paid orders and unpaid balances
steps: If orders were still partially paid at the end of the reporting period, the report adds notes about them.
Click a partially paid order link or an unpaid balance link to see the details.
entries.quote: If any orders remained partially paid at the end of the reporting period, the report adds notes about them.

entries.title: Run the Discounts report on a device
steps: You need the Access Reporting > View Discounts report permission.
On the device, open the Reporting app.
Tap Discounts. The report covers this business day by default.
To change the period, tap Date Range at the top right, pick an option or Custom, and tap Done.
To print, tap Print.
entries.quote: In the Reporting app, tap Discounts.

entries.title: Change when the reporting day starts
steps: Log in to your Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Reporting.
Under Reporting hours, select Edit.
Select a Start of day time.
Select Save.
The default start is 12:00 AM and a day spans 24 hours.
entries.quote: Customizing your reporting hours ensures your daily sales report aligns with your actual business hours.

entries.title: Show tip payouts from the cash drawer on cash reports
steps: Log in to your Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Reporting.
Under Customize reports, select Edit and turn on the Show tips payout on Cash report toggle.
Select Save.
entries.quote: If you pay out employee tips directly from your cash drawer, enable this setting to ensure your Sales Overview reflects an accurate "Expected Deposit" amount.

entries.title: A requested report can no longer be exported
steps: A requested report must be exported within 7 days.
Run or request the report again.
entries.quote: If you don't export the requested report within 7 days, run or request the report again.

entries.title: 'Choose your currency' screen during a card payment
steps: This is Dynamic Currency Conversion. It appears when the device detects a foreign-issued Mastercard or Visa card that is eligible.
The screen shows totals in both currencies, the exchange rate and the service fee.
The customer chooses US dollars or their card's currency. Never choose for them or steer them.
Select the option the customer wants. The payment then runs in that currency.
You are always funded in USD.
entries.quote: If your Clover device identifies a card as eligible for DCC, a Choose your currency screen is displayed to the customer.

entries.title: Receipt is required when a customer pays in a foreign currency
steps: If the customer chooses to pay in a foreign currency you must give a DCC transaction receipt.
It does not have to be printed: a text receipt is acceptable if the customer prefers.
entries.quote: A printed receipt is not required; a text receipt is acceptable based on customer preference.

entries.title: Customer does not want currency conversion
steps: If the customer declines the conversion offer, complete the transaction in US dollars.
entries.quote: If the customer declines the DCC offer, the transaction must be completed in US dollars.

entries.title: Take a Klarna payment
steps: Klarna must be enabled as a tender on the device or dashboard.
Enter the sale and start checkout.
Select the Klarna tender. A Klarna QR code and the amount appear on the device.
The customer scans the QR code with the Klarna app. The Clover device shows a processing screen.
The customer checks the amount and picks a payment plan in the Klarna app.
When Klarna authorizes, the Clover device shows payment approved and the receipt options.
entries.quote: Select the Klarna tender. A Klarna QR code and the purchase amount appear on the device.

entries.title: Klarna does not show for a large order
steps: The Klarna tender shows at checkout only when the order total is $10,000 or less.
entries.quote: Klarna tender displays at checkout when the order total is $10,000 or less.

entries.title: An approved Klarna payment cannot be cancelled
steps: Once approved, a Klarna payment cannot be cancelled.
Issue a refund instead.
entries.quote: You cannot cancel an approved payment; issue a refund instead.

entries.title: Take a quick sale in the Clover Go app
steps: Tap New Sale (bottom of the home screen on a phone, left side on a tablet).
Enter the full sale amount including taxes and fees, and tap Checkout.
Enter an invoice number if asked (on by default).
If you are using a card reader, you can take the card payment now.
Otherwise tap Take Payment.
Add a payment note if asked and tap Done.
On the Checkout screen tap Enter card manually, then scan or key in the card.
Tap Complete Transaction.
If tips are on, enter a tip and tap Approve payment.
Select a receipt option.
entries.quote: Enter the full sale amount, including taxes and other fees, and tap Checkout.

entries.title: Key in a card in the Go app when the customer is not present
steps: On the Checkout screen, tap Enter card manually.
The app assumes the physical card is present. If you do not have the card in hand, turn off Card Present.
Key in the card number, expiration date, CVV, zip code and the house or building number.
Tap Complete Transaction.
entries.quote: If you don't have the physical card, key in the card number, expiration date, CVV, and zip code, and the house or building number.

entries.title: Scan a card with the phone camera in the Go app
steps: On the Checkout screen, tap Enter card manually.
If you have the physical card, tap Scan and follow the prompt to take a photo of the card.
Card photos are not stored on the device or in the app.
Tap Complete Transaction.
entries.quote: (Card photos are not stored on your device or in the app.)

entries.title: Go app only shows the quick sale screen, no items
steps: The New Sale screen defaults to either quick sale or itemized sale depending on your service plan.
To itemize sales, the plan needs upgrading. Clover says to contact your business consultant.
entries.quote: If you see only the quick sale screen, and want to itemize sales, contact your business consultant to upgrade your service plan.

entries.title: Take an itemized sale in the Go app on a phone
steps: Open the Clover Go G2 app and tap New Sale.
Tap items to add them. Tap an item again to add one more.
Tap Checkout, then tap Take payment.
Enter an invoice number and tap Done.
Select a payment type.
Use the card reader, or tap Scan to scan the card, enter the other required information and tap Complete Transaction.
Select a receipt option.
entries.quote: Tap an item repeatedly to increment the item count by one (1).

entries.title: Take an itemized sale in the Go app on a tablet
steps: Tap New Sale and add items, then tap Checkout.
Enter an invoice number and tap Next.
Select a payment type.
Use the card reader, or enter the card information and tap Charge.
If the card is not in hand, deselect 'This is an in-person transaction.'
If you accept tips, enter the tip amount and tap Next.
Hand the tablet to the customer to sign the screen.
Tap Done and select a receipt option.
entries.quote: Hand the tablet to your customer and have them sign the screen.

entries.title: Cannot itemize a sale in the Go app: no items
steps: To itemize orders the inventory must contain at least one item.
Until then you can still take a sale by entering the full amount with the Custom option.
Add items to your inventory first.
entries.quote: To itemize orders, your inventory must contain at least one item.

entries.title: Which payment types show in the Go app
steps: The payment methods shown on screen are the tender types you selected on the dashboard.
entries.quote: The payment methods displayed onscreen reflect the tender types you previously selected on the Dashboard.

entries.title: Add a custom item in the Go app
steps: In an order, tap Custom Item.
Enter the price.
Optionally enter a name and tap Return.
Optionally tap More Options to save it to inventory or apply discounts, taxes and fees.
Carry on adding items, or tap Checkout.
entries.quote: In an existing order, tap Custom Item.

entries.title: Apply a discount in the Go app
steps: Do this after creating the order and before checkout.
Item discount: tap the item on the Checkout screen and select a saved discount or enter a custom percentage or dollar amount.
Order discount: tap Order Options, tap Apply order discount and select the discount.
Tap Take payment.
entries.quote: Order discount. Tap Order Options, then tap Apply order discount to display Order discounts options

entries.title: Add a customer to a Go app sale so the receipt details fill in
steps: On the New Sale screen, tap the menu icon to the right of Check out.
Tap Select next to Customer.
Pick an existing customer or tap New customer.
After checkout, tapping Email or Text on the Payment complete screen fills in the customer's details.
Tap Send.
entries.quote: Tap Select next to Customer.

entries.title: Stop the Go app asking for an invoice number
steps: In the Go G2 app, open the More menu and tap Settings.
Under Transactions, tap the button next to Enable invoice # to turn it off.
entries.quote: On by default, tap the button next to Enable invoice # to turn it off.

entries.title: Stop the Go app asking for a payment note
steps: In the Go G2 app, open the More menu and tap Settings.
